Recommended Highlights This Week

1. Trevor Noah – 3, 4 and 5 November, The Star Theatre

2. LANY: soft world tour – 4 November, Singapore Indoor Stadium

3. Deepavali in Little India – Sunday 8 November, with the Festival Village closing that night

4. Petra – opened 24 October, Harding Road, Dempsey Hill

5. Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism, and the Silk Road – Asian Civilisations Museum, through 7 March 2027

Events & Festivals

Overall Summary

A week led by three evenings of live entertainment and the build to Deepavali. Trevor Noah performs at The Star Theatre from Tuesday to Thursday, yung kai plays Capitol Theatre on Tuesday and LANY take the Singapore Indoor Stadium on Wednesday, before Little India celebrates Deepavali on Sunday 8 November. Several exhibitions continue, and teamLab: Infinite Existence closes on Sunday.

Trevor Noah

Trevor Noah brings his stand-up show to The Star Theatre for three nights, as part of Just For Laughs Singapore.

Event Date: Tuesday 3, Wednesday 4 and Thursday 5 November 2026
Location: The Star Theatre, #04-01 The Star Performing Arts Centre, 1 Vista Exchange Green, Singapore 138617
Admission: Ticketed through SISTIC
Best For: Comedy fans, groups and corporate guests looking for an evening out

Concierge Recommendation: Guests should confirm the show time on their ticket before arranging dinner. The Star Theatre is a short walk from Buona Vista MRT, and taxi and ride-hailing queues build quickly after the show, so return transport is best arranged in advance.

LANY: soft world tour

American pop band LANY bring their soft world tour to the Singapore Indoor Stadium for one night.

Event Date: Wednesday 4 November 2026, 8:00pm (doors 6:30pm for general admission and Category 1 standing; 6:00pm for VIP)
Location: Singapore Indoor Stadium, Singapore Sports Hub, 2 Stadium Walk, Singapore 397691
Admission: Ticketed through Ticketmaster Singapore; children under 6 are not admitted
Best For: Pop and indie fans, couples and young groups

Concierge Recommendation: Guests should leave the hotel by 5:30pm for a 6:30pm door time. The Stadium MRT station is a short walk from the venue, and ride-hailing demand is high at the end of the show, so a pre-booked car is the safer return.

yung kai: Asia Tour 2026

yung kai brings his Asia Tour to Capitol Theatre for one night in Singapore.

Event Date: Tuesday 3 November 2026, 8:00pm–10:30pm
Location: Capitol Theatre, 17 Stamford Road, Singapore 178907
Admission: Ticketed; promoted by Live Nation Singapore
Best For: Younger guests and R&B and pop fans

Concierge Recommendation: Capitol Theatre is a short walk from City Hall MRT, so guests can dine in the Civic District beforehand and walk back to the hotel area by taxi from Stamford Road.

Deepavali in Little India

Deepavali falls on Sunday 8 November. Little India has been lit since 3 October, and the Festival Village on Campbell Lane closes with the festival.

Event Date: Festival lights nightly, 7:00pm–midnight, through Deepavali on Sunday 8 November 2026; Festival Village from 7:00pm, final night 8 November
Location: Serangoon Road and Campbell Lane, Little India; Indian Heritage Centre, 5 Campbell Lane (Deepavali Open House through 8 November, 10:00am–6:00pm)
Admission: Free
Best For: All guests, families and photographers

Concierge Recommendation: Deepavali evening is the busiest of the season. Guests should arrive before 6:00pm, and taxis are best arranged to drop off at the edge of Little India, since road closures apply on Sunday. Little India MRT is the easiest approach.

Continuing This Week

These exhibitions and attractions remain open through the coming days.

Sacred Caves: Dunhuang, Buddhism, and the Silk Road – Asian Civilisations Museum, 1 Empress Place. Through 7 March 2027, daily 10:00am–7:00pm; Fridays until 9:00pm. All-access ticket required.
teamLab: Infinite Existence – Supper House, 37 Keppel Road, #04-02. Closes Sunday 8 November 2026. Thursday to Saturday 12:00pm–7:00pm; Sunday 12:00pm–5:00pm; closed Monday to Wednesday. Free.
Fan Chang Tien: Rhythm of the Southern Brush – Wu Guanzhong Gallery, Level 4, City Hall Wing, National Gallery Singapore. Through 31 January 2027, daily 10:00am–7:00pm.
Toy Story | PEACEMINUSONE: THE FIRST FAN pop-up – CQ @ Clarke Quay, 3A River Valley Road, #01-02. Through 11 November 2026. Access pass $12; advance reservation required.

Concierge Recommendation: Sacred Caves and Fan Chang Tien pair well on a Civic District day. teamLab is closed Monday to Wednesday, so it can be visited only from Thursday 5 to Sunday 8 November before it closes.

Also This Week

  • Toy Story High Tea at SKAI – 1 to 30 November 2026.

  • Dopamine Land Singapore – 1 November to 31 December 2026, tickets from SGD 22.

  • Haw Ror Villa 5 – Haw Par Villa, 262 Pasir Panjang Road. Selected nights through 15 November, 6:30pm–midnight. Full-face masks are not allowed.

  • Disney Garden of Wonder – Floral Fantasy, Gardens by the Bay. Daily 10:00am–9:00pm (last admission 8:30pm), through 14 March 2027. Non-residents $24 adult, $16 child.

  • Jurassic World: The Experience – Cloud Forest, Gardens by the Bay. Daily 9:00am–9:00pm. Non-residents $46 adult, $32 child, including Flower Dome.

  • Singapore International Photography Festival, 10th edition – exhibitions at Lorong 24 Geylang and SingPost Geylang, through 31 January 2027. Festival Pass $50 ($40 concession); single venues $15 to $20.

  • Horizon of Khufu: Journey in Ancient Egypt – Parkview Square, 600 North Bridge Road. A VR experience, daily 10:00am–6:00pm, until 2 April 2027. $35 adult, $29 child under 8.

  • Singapore History Gallery – National Museum of Singapore. The reopened permanent gallery is open daily, 10:00am–7:00pm.

Restaurants & Bars

Petra

A Mediterranean restaurant on Dempsey Hill with a Levantine lean, which opened on Saturday 24 October. The menu runs from mezze to wood-fired seafood and grilled meats, with a patisserie section. Executive chef Anas Shami was previously at Aniba, and consultant chef Dawid Nowosadzki has worked in the Ottolenghi group, including NOPI.

Location: Level 1, 40C Harding Road, Dempsey Hill, Singapore 249548
Hours: Monday to Thursday 11:30am–3:00pm and 5:30pm–10:30pm; Friday 11:30am–3:00pm and 5:30pm–11:00pm; Saturday 11:30am–11:00pm; Sunday 11:30am–10:30pm
Reservations: Online via SevenRooms, or +65 8876 5823. Private dinners and long-table events are also offered
At Launch: Hamachi tartare, hummus and muhallabia (a milk pudding)

Concierge Recommendation: A new dinner option for guests who want Dempsey Hill, with all-day service at weekends. Reserve ahead, particularly for Friday and Saturday evenings.

Kiap Kiap Chicken Club & Bar

A fried chicken bar in Bugis that keeps late hours, with a menu that mixes fried chicken with Asian-leaning sides and cocktails.

Location: #02-15, 1 Liang Seah Street, Singapore 189022
Hours: Daily 5:30pm–1:00am; Friday and Saturday until 2:00am
Opened: October 2026
Signature: Duck fat mala fried chicken, $14; Jenny's Udon, from $12; King's truffle poutine, $20; banana pudding, $6; kaya daiquiri, $20

Concierge Recommendation: A casual late-night choice for guests after the theatre or a Bugis evening. Liang Seah Street is closed to traffic from 6:30pm to midnight on Friday to Sunday, so guests should be dropped off at the end of the street.

Gamja

A Korean gamjatang specialist on Boon Tat Street in the Telok Ayer area, serving white and traditional gamjatang alongside kimchi jeon and a house potato salad.

Location: 21 Boon Tat Street, Singapore 069620
Hours: Daily 11:00am–3:00pm and 5:30pm–11:00pm
Signature: White gamjatang; traditional pork gamjatang; signature potato salad; kimchi jeon. Lunch gamjatang from $15.80; sharing gamjatang from $53; sides from $8.80; BBQ from $18
Note: The traditional gamjatang is made with pork

Concierge Recommendation: A warming, good-value option for guests who want Korean comfort food near Telok Ayer and Raffles Place.

Moutai House

A three-storey Moutai destination in The Fullerton Waterboat House, bringing together an experiential centre, a Chinese restaurant run with the Imperial Treasure group, and a rooftop bar. The collection runs to more than 300 Moutai labels.

Location: The Fullerton Waterboat House, 3 Fullerton Road, Singapore 049215
Opening: Announced for late October 2026
Experiential Centre: Daily 10:00am–10:00pm, covering Moutai’s history and production
Imperial Treasure Moutai House (second floor): Huaiyang and Guizhou cuisine. Daily 11:00am–3:00pm and 6:00pm–10:00pm
SOHAUS (rooftop bar, third floor): Tuesday to Saturday 5:00pm–midnight; signature Moutai cocktails with skyline and waterfront views

Concierge Recommendation: Of interest to guests who enjoy baijiu or Chinese fine dining. Check moutaihouse.sg for current opening status and reservations before booking on a guest's behalf.

Hotel & Hospitality News

DoubleTree by Hilton Singapore Robertson Quay, at 401 Havelock Road with 344 rooms and suites, opened at the end of September. Its all-day restaurant, SAUS, began lunch and dinner service on Sunday 1 November. There are no other hotel openings or leadership appointments to report this week.

Transport & Operational Updates

Overnight expressway work this week: the CTE (City) Exit 8A slip road towards PIE (Tuas) is closed from 12:00am to 5:00am on Saturday 7 November, for construction of a pedestrian and cycling link.

Weekend and evening closures to note: Little India roads, including Lembu Road, Kerbau Road, Chander Road, Dunlop Street and Birch Road, close on Sundays from 12:00pm to midnight, which includes Deepavali on 8 November. Liang Seah Street is closed to traffic from 6:30pm to midnight from Friday to Sunday. Holland Village and Kampong Gelam (Bussorah Street, Baghdad Street, Haji Lane and Bali Lane) also restrict traffic on weekend evenings, so drop-offs should be planned at the edge of each area.

Expect higher taxi and ride-hailing demand around The Star Theatre at the end of Trevor Noah on Tuesday 3, Wednesday 4 and Thursday 5 November, around the Singapore Indoor Stadium at the end of LANY on Wednesday 4 November (8:00pm start), and in Little India on the evening of Deepavali, Sunday 8 November.

Suggested Itineraries

A Deepavali Sunday in Little India

Morning: Indian Heritage Centre Deepavali Open House, 5 Campbell Lane, from 10:00am (free).

Afternoon: Walk Serangoon Road and its shops before the evening crowds; road closures apply from 12:00pm.

Evening: The Deepavali lights (7:00pm–midnight) and the Festival Village on Campbell Lane (from 7:00pm), which closes that night.

Tip: Guests should be dropped off at the edge of Little India and walk in, and the return taxi is best arranged for before 10:00pm.

A Gallery Day and Trevor Noah

Morning: Sacred Caves at the Asian Civilisations Museum, from 10:00am.

Afternoon: Fan Chang Tien at the National Gallery Singapore, open until 7:00pm.

Evening: Trevor Noah at The Star Theatre on Thursday 5 November.

Tip: Thursday is the final night of the Singapore run, and the transfer from the Civic District to Buona Vista should allow at least 40 minutes.

Dempsey Lunch and LANY

Afternoon: Lunch at Petra on Dempsey Hill on Wednesday 4 November, open 11:30am–3:00pm.

Evening: LANY at the Singapore Indoor Stadium, 8:00pm, with doors from 6:30pm.

Tip: Guests should leave by 5:30pm, and a pre-booked car for the return is advised given post-concert demand.

Quick Reference

Best Comedy This Week: Trevor Noah (The Star Theatre, 3 to 5 November)

Best Concert This Week: LANY (Singapore Indoor Stadium, 4 November)

Best Cultural Pick: Deepavali in Little India (lights nightly, Deepavali on 8 November)

Best Free Pick: Deepavali lights, Serangoon Road, Little India (nightly 7:00pm–midnight)

Best Exhibition: Sacred Caves (Asian Civilisations Museum, through 7 March 2027)

Best Hotel Dining Pick: Golden Autumn Hairy Crab at Shang Palace (through 30 November)

Best New Opening: Petra (Harding Road, Dempsey Hill, opened 24 October)

Looking Ahead: My Chemical Romance at the Singapore Indoor Stadium on 10 and 11 November; White Truffle Season at Waterfall Ristorante Italiano from 10 November; Singapore Writers Festival from 13 to 22 November; Joe Hisaishi on 14 November
